dropped.candidate: Phase 1 lead (web-app.json): patch-inspector.ts pixelsPerHoopForDrum / perHoopPixelCount / hoopPixelSpan share a (drum, kit, …) tuple => missing hoop-geometry value object
dropped.why_rejected: Read all three at apps/web/src/lib/app/docks/patch-inspector.ts:80, :89, :149. The shared tuple is (drum, kit) — TWO params, below this lens's >=3 threshold. Worse, the third function does not even share it: hoopPixelSpan(routing: OutputConfig[], ref: {drumId,hoop}, pixelsForHoop) takes a completely different shape and ALREADY uses an object for its address. perHoopPixelCount's third param (hoopIndex) is the varying argument, not a co-traveller. A (drum, kit) value object would be a wrapper around two things the caller already holds side by side with no third member to justify it. Not a clump.

dropped.candidate: Phase 1 lead (web-triggerlab.json): trigger-routing.ts DrumTransformPartial / KitGlobalPartial / HoopConfigPartial / OutputPartial and their mirrored store setters => one Project-patch operation split four ways
dropped.why_rejected: Read apps/web/src/lib/trigger-lab/store/trigger-routing.ts (145 lines). Every apply* function is (project, partial) or (project, drumId, hoopIndex, partial) — the four Partial types are DISJOINT field sets (transform geometry vs kit globals vs per-hoop pixel count vs output protocol), not one tuple recurring. This is a parallel-structure / mutation-parity observation, which is a different lens's territory. There is no set of >=3 parameters travelling together across >=3 sites here; unifying the four Partials would merge four correctly-narrow types into one wide one, which INCREASES interface surface. Actively wrong to fix.

dropped.candidate: Phase 1 lead (server.json): main.ts boot() and stateMessage() pass the same (host, voiceHost, clients, autosavers x3, tunnelControl, monitor) bag => an unnamed 'ServerContext'
dropped.why_rejected: Half wrong, and I kept only the half that survived. The bag IS already named twice: BootDeps (boot.ts:12-43, fully documented) and ClientMessageDeps (client-message.ts:85+). Both are single object params, not positional clumps, so the headline claim ('never been named') is false. stateMessage() at main.ts:446 takes NO parameters at all — it closes over module scope. What did survive is narrower: the three sibling Autosaver fields inside those bags, which I filed as its own finding. Rejecting the broad 'ServerContext' framing: merging BootDeps and ClientMessageDeps would couple the lifecycle surface to the message surface and increase what each consumer can reach.

dropped.candidate: Mechanical hit: canvas/elements.ts stripesAt / circleAt / gradientAt / polygonAt / checkerAt / noiseAt / elementAt all take (u, v[, t], el) — 7 functions, top clump by raw count
dropped.why_rejected: Genuine co-travel, but the fix is net-negative here and I will not file it. These are per-pixel-per-element renderers on the deepest inner loop in the repo (sceneColorAt at elements.ts:171 calls elementAt for every element at every pixel of every frame). AGENTS.md forbids allocation on the render loop; packaging (u,v,t) into a SamplePoint object either allocates per call or forces a mutable shared scratch that reintroduces the hidden-global-state hazard the same doc bans ('effects must be pure functions of RenderContext, no hidden global state'). The params are also maximally distinguishable in practice — u and v are a coordinate pair everyone reads as one idiom, and the arity is 3-4, not 8. Cost exceeds benefit.

dropped.candidate: Mechanical hit: sendPlain(res, status, body) duplicated at http/native-midi.ts:32 and http/host-event.ts:68, plus sendJson(res, status, body) at http/update-status.ts:45
dropped.why_rejected: The tuple recurs, but the defect is duplicated-helper, not a missing type: (res, status, body) is the standard Node http response idiom and no value object wants to be born from it. The right fix is one shared `respond()` in a server http util, which belongs to the duplication lens, not mine. Filing it here would collide on dedup with that lens's better-framed version.

dropped.candidate: Mechanical hit: pnum / pstr / pbool in packages/core/src/effects/types.ts:77-89 all take (params, key, fallback)
dropped.why_rejected: Three params travelling across three functions, so it trips the mechanical bar — but this is a typed-accessor family, the intended shape. `params` is the receiver, `key` selects, `fallback` is the per-call default; there is no tuple with independent identity. Bundling them would produce `pnum(params, {key, fallback})`, which is strictly worse ergonomics for a hot accessor. Correct as written.

dropped.candidate: Mechanical hit: setHoopConfig(drumId, hoopIndex, partial) at store.svelte.ts:1883, voice-engine-host.ts:242 and engine.ts:334; identifyHoop(drumId, hoop, durationMs) at engine-host.ts:195 and voice-engine-host.ts:411
dropped.why_rejected: These are cross-layer delegation chains (web store -> server host -> core engine) forwarding the same call, not independent sites that co-evolved a tuple. The co-travelling part is (drumId, hoopIndex) — TWO members, below threshold; the third slot differs per function (partial vs durationMs). A HoopRef value object would add an exported type to three packages to save one param at each hop. Interface delta would be 'increases'. Not worth it.

dropped.candidate: Mechanical hit: color.ts hsvToRgb(h,s,v) / hsvToHex(h,s,v) and rgbToHsv(r,g,b) / rgbToHex(r,g,b)
dropped.why_rejected: Colour component triples are the universal idiom and both modules already expose object-returning counterparts where an object is warranted. Introducing Hsv/Rgb params would force allocation at ~every pixel in the effects layer (hsvToRgb is called inside every element renderer in canvas/elements.ts). Same hot-path reasoning as the elements.ts rejection; also, ColorSwatch.svelte already imports an `Hsv` type for the places where the object form belongs.

items.claim: The tuple {timeMs, bpm, cc, osc, notes} travels through the voice path under three names and one un-named positional spread. compositor.ts:80 already declares `type FrameModCtx = Omit<ModSampleCtx,'phase'>` — exactly this tuple — and modCtxFor() consumes it, yet the sibling export applyEffectiveParams (line 61) takes the same five members as bare positional params (v, timeMs, bpm, cc?, osc?, notes?) and re-bundles them internally. CompositorFrame (line 154) carries the same live-table trio (cc/osc/notes) plus transport, and render() at line 180 hand-copies it into a FrameModCtx literal. The clump has a name; three of four sites refuse to use it.

evidence.detail: packages/core/src/voice/compositor.ts:61 — `export function applyEffectiveParams(v: Voice, timeMs: number, bpm: number, cc?: CcTable, osc?: OscTable, notes?: NoteTable): ParamValues`; line 80 in the SAME file — `type FrameModCtx = Omit<ModSampleCtx, 'phase'>` which is precisely {timeMs,bpm,cc,osc,notes}.

evidence.command: grep -rn "notes?: NoteTable|osc?: OscTable|cc?: CcTable" packages apps
evidence.detail: Only 3 declaration sites, and they are the three names of the same tuple: compositor.ts:61 (positional), compositor.ts:160-164 (CompositorFrame), modulation.ts:198-203 (ModSampleCtx).

packages/core/src/voice/engine.ts:711 — `applyEffectiveParams(v, this.timeMs, this.bpm, this.ccTable, this.oscTable, this.noteTable)` — the engine holds all five as sibling fields and explodes them at the call.

items.proposed_fix: Export FrameModCtx from compositor.ts (or better, move it beside ModSampleCtx in modulation.ts as the canonical 'frame-wide modulation context'). Change applyEffectiveParams to `(v: Voice, frame: FrameModCtx)`. Have VoiceEngine hold one FrameModCtx field it mutates in place per tick (zero-alloc, same as today's scratch discipline) and pass it to both applyEffectiveParams and the compositor. Make CompositorFrame embed it: `{ dt, transport, mod: FrameModCtx }` or leave CompositorFrame as the host-facing shape and have render() keep its single conversion.

removes_failure_path.justification: Pure signature reshaping; the optional-table neutrality (absent cc/osc/notes => neutral sample) is preserved by keeping the fields optional on FrameModCtx, which they already are on ModSampleCtx.

steps: pnpm typecheck — the compiler enumerates every applyEffectiveParams call site (engine.ts:711 plus modulation.test.ts / modulation-graph.test.ts)
pnpm test --filter @ledrums/core — modulation.test.ts and modulation-graph.test.ts pin the sweep semantics and must stay green unchanged in expectation

items.claim: Eight design-system primitives each independently declare the identical four-member control contract — `onChange?: (v: T) => void; disabled?: boolean; ariaLabel?: string; class?: string` — with no shared base type. There is no compiler force keeping them aligned: SearchField.svelte already drifted (it has onChange/ariaLabel/class but no `disabled`, line 6-11), and IconButton.svelte uses `label` where the others use `ariaLabel` (line 13-17). Changing the control contract (e.g. adding a `required`/`invalid` a11y flag, or renaming ariaLabel) is an eight-file manual sweep the type system cannot check.

evidence.command: for f in $(grep -rl 'type Props' --include='*.svelte' apps/web/src/lib); do grep -q onChange $f && grep -q 'disabled?: boolean' $f && grep -q 'ariaLabel?: string' $f && grep -q 'class?: string' $f && echo $f; done
evidence.detail: Returns exactly 8 files: ColorSwatch, SegmentedControl, Switch, Toggle, TextField, Select, Slider, EasePicker — all four members present, all declared inline.

apps/web/src/lib/ui/Switch.svelte:6-14 declares the full four and destructures `class: klass`; apps/web/src/lib/ui/SearchField.svelte:6-14 declares only three (no `disabled`) — the drift is already present.

items.proposed_fix: Add `export type ControlProps<T> = { onChange?: (v: T) => void; disabled?: boolean; ariaLabel?: string; class?: string }` to a new apps/web/src/lib/ui/control-props.ts (or theme-tokens.ts's sibling). Each primitive becomes `type Props = ControlProps<number> & { value: number; ... }`. Backfill `disabled` on SearchField in the same change and add the type to the styleguide entry per AGENTS.md's use-or-extend rule.

removes_failure_path.justification: Pure type extraction; every prop keeps its optionality and its default at the destructuring site. No guard, validation or fallback is touched.

steps: pnpm typecheck — svelte-check resolves every consumer of the 8 primitives; any prop dropped or renamed surfaces as an error
pnpm test — Slider.test.ts, ColorSwatch.test.ts, ListItem.test.ts, EditableRow.test.ts exercise the props surface
pnpm design-system then diff docs/design-system.html to confirm the styleguide still renders every primitive

items.claim: Three functions carry the identical 8-slot positional tuple (state, graph|plan, pad, startIds|childIds, ctx, viaPrefix, seen, draft) and do nothing but forward it to each other: evalGraphGen3 -> evalGraphGen3FromPlan (line 269), evalChildren -> evalGraphGen3From -> evalGraphGen3FromPlan (lines 625, 274). Six of the eight members (state, graph/plan, pad, ctx, viaPrefix, seen) are one traversal cursor; only startIds and draft vary per hop. Eight same-shaped positional args across three hops is the classic silent-transposition hazard — `seen` and `viaPrefix` are both invariant-carrying and adjacent, and `viaPrefix: string` sits next to `pad: string`, so a swapped pair type-checks cleanly.

evidence.detail: packages/core/src/voice/eval-graph.ts:262-275 and :277-286 — the two signatures differ only in `graph: TriggerGraph` vs `plan: RenderPlan`; every other slot is identical in name, order and type.

packages/core/src/voice/eval-graph.ts:615-626 — the exported `evalChildren` re-lists all 8 and its whole body is a single forwarding call.

Signatures become `evalGraphGen3FromPlan(cursor: EvalCursor, plan: RenderPlan, startIds: readonly string[], draft: PlayDraft | null)` and likewise for the graph variant. Keep `evalChildren`'s exported signature intact as the public seam (it is called from the engine's pending-fire drain) and have it construct the cursor — that confines the churn to one file.

items.claim: `fromId, toId, fromPort?, toPort?` travel as a four-slot positional tuple through classifyConnection, classifyReconnect, canConnect, canReconnect and the private sameSlot helper, and are re-spelled at 8 call sites. Two of the four slots are `string | undefined` in adjacent positions, so a from/to port transposition type-checks. TriggerGraphView.svelte:565 and :573 deliberately swap fromId/toId to validate a reverse drag (`canConnect(g, toId, from.nodeId, undefined, toPort)`) — exactly the manoeuvre a named `WireEnds { from, to, fromPort?, toPort? }` would make legible and a positional tuple makes an easy transposition bug.

evidence.detail: 17 hits across 3 non-test files; 5 declaration sites all carrying the identical 4-slot tail, 8 call sites re-spelling it, including 5 in TriggerGraphView.svelte alone.

apps/web/src/lib/trigger-lab/store/graph-wiring.ts:150 and :165 — canConnect/canReconnect are pure pass-throughs whose entire body is the same 4-slot forward: `classifyConnection(graph, fromId, toId, fromPort, toPort) === null`.

items.proposed_fix: Add `export interface WireEnds { from: string; to: string; fromPort?: string; toPort?: ToPort }` in graph-wiring.ts. Signatures become `classifyConnection(graph: TriggerGraph, w: WireEnds)`, `classifyReconnect(graph, edgeId, w)`, and the two `can*` verdicts likewise. Call sites in TriggerGraphView.svelte become named-field literals, which makes the deliberate reverse-drag swap self-documenting.

removes_failure_path.justification: The direction/duplicate/cycle precedence, the self-loop check and the pure+total 'never throws on unknown ids' contract are all inside the bodies and are not touched.

steps: pnpm typecheck

items.claim: `autosaver`, `showLibraryAutosaver`, `songLibraryAutosaver` are declared as three sibling `Autosaver` fields on BootDeps (boot.ts:28-30) and again on ClientMessageDeps (client-message.ts:89-91), passed as three arguments at both main.ts:622-624 and main.ts:793-795, and flushed as three parallel calls at boot.ts:125-127. They are three same-typed members that are never used apart: every consumer either markDirty()s one of them or flushes all three. A fourth persisted slot (a very likely addition) is a five-file edit today, and the shutdown flush at boot.ts:125-127 is the exact place a forgotten fourth autosaver would silently lose the last edit.

evidence.detail: 20 non-test hits: 2 construction sites (main.ts:190, :201), 2 interface declarations (boot.ts:29-30, client-message.ts:90-91), 2 pass-through call sites (main.ts:623-624, :794-795), 2 destructures (client-message.ts:166-167), 4 markDirty call sites, plus the boot.ts:126-127 flush pair.

apps/server/src/boot.ts:124-128 — shutdown awaits `deps.autosaver.flush()`, `deps.showLibraryAutosaver.flush()`, `deps.songLibraryAutosaver.flush()` as three hand-written lines rather than iterating a collection.

items.proposed_fix: Replace the three fields with one `Autosavers { project: Autosaver; showLibrary: Autosaver; songLibrary: Autosaver }` (or, given every consumer only calls markDirty/flush, a `readonly Autosaver[]` for the flush path plus named accessors). BootDeps and ClientMessageDeps each shed two fields; the shutdown flush becomes `Object.values(deps.autosavers).map(a => a.flush().catch(() => {}))`, which cannot forget a future member.

removes_failure_path.justification: The `.catch(() => {})` per-flush swallow at boot.ts:125-127 must be preserved verbatim in the iterated form; nothing is removed, and the change makes the flush set harder to under-populate.

items.claim: `{drumId, slot}` is the repo's trigger address, and it already exists as an object in four separate core schemas (midiNoteMapSchema:73-77, oscMapSchema:80-84, declaredZoneSchema:90-93, triggerBindingSchema:108-110) with no shared base — each re-declares `drumId: z.string(), slot: slotSchema`. In the web layer it is then exploded into positional params across seven functions in patch-inspector.ts, whose bodies immediately re-materialise it: `[...rest, { note, drumId, slot }]` (line 124), `{ ...map, zones: [...zones, { drumId, slot }] }` (line 274). moveZoneSlot (line 320) juggles four such addresses positionally in one function. Both `slot: number` params of `moveZoneSlot(map, drumId, oldSlot, newSlot)` are indistinguishable to the compiler.

items.claim: `PixelRange { start, end }` is an exported core type (modifiers/types.ts:31) used by applyModifierChain and produced by `pixelRangesFor()`.
